## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Ice Temperature Reading
where: RinkService (uses), src/business/rinkService.ts, component business

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: A and B are the same concept. RinkService (node 21c65604dec116b1, src/business/rinkService.ts) builds a reading with `this.temperatures.add({ temperatureC: temp, at });`. TemperatureRepository (node 50b830f77ad06c02, src/persistence/temperatureRepository.ts) stores these as `private readings: TemperatureReading[] = [];`. The graph shows TemperatureRepository is constructor-injected into RinkService and called by RinkService.recordTemperature, so `this.temperatures` is almost certainly that repository. The service creates the ice temperature reading and the repository stores it; "Ice" in A's name only adds rink context. Confidence is not total because the repository's add method and the TemperatureReading type definition are not visible.
